text: Someone assumed Claude would approve or reject a new client. It doesn't, it scores the file against a rules grid. So, does Claude score a new client's KYC file against the firm's rules? A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is called kick rules. It's just one file skill MD written in plain language no hidden logic. Claude reads the file then acts on what it says. The file is the whole program. Inside the instructions are steps and Claude runs them in order. First, read the parsed onboarding record then apply each rule from the grid in order then hand back the ratings and the flags. No

Branching unless a step itself tells it to branch. This particular skill runs after another skill has already parsed a new client's onboarding record into structured fields. Kick rules job is to apply the firm's KYC and AML rules grid to that record, assign a risk rating, list every rule outcome with the rule that produced it and flag anything missing or worth escalating. It doesn't decide whether to accept the client. It scores the file and routes it. The accept or reject call stays with a person. Kick rules scores a client file against the firm's own rules and flags what needs a person. It never decides whether to accept anyone.

Your turn, paste this into Claude. I have a set of compliance rules and a record I need to check against them. Before you tell me whether it passes, walk me through each rule, whether the record satisfies it and what's missing then hand the actual decision back to me. That's the same order kick rules follows, score against the rules, flag what's missing and leave the decision to a person. It scores and routes, it doesn't decide. Lay 'em in for bear.
